body:
Source: the 1.12.0 release audits. `scripts/release-audit-collect.mjs` runs every subprocess through tryRun, which calls execFileSync with the default 1 MiB maxBuffer. The open-issue fetch (`gh issue list --limit 500 --json ...,body,...`) now returns about 1.1 MB, so execFileSync throws ENOBUFS and every audit records the backlog as unconsultable. The recorded reason is `gh issue list failed: ` with nothing after it, because tryRun prefers err.stderr through `??`, and an empty-string stderr wins over err.message. Both audits on 2026-10-09 ran with GitHub issues untriaged for this reason.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. tryRun gives its child a maxBuffer large enough for the 500-issue fetch with full bodies (64 MiB, named as a constant).
2. When a child fails with empty stderr, the recorded reason falls back to the error message (for example ENOBUFS), never an empty string.
3. The fail-closed behaviour is unchanged: a failed fetch is still recorded as unconsultable, never as an empty backlog.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 tryRun passes a maxBuffer of at least 64 MiB to its runner; a test with an injected runner asserts it. verify: `node --test scripts/test/release-audit-collect.test.mjs`
- AC2 A runner that throws with stderr '' and message 'spawnSync gh ENOBUFS' yields an unconsultable reason containing ENOBUFS. verify: `node --test scripts/test/release-audit-collect.test.mjs`
- AC3 The existing collector tests stay green. verify: `node --test scripts/test/release-audit-*.test.mjs`

OUT OF SCOPE: changing ISSUE_FETCH_LIMIT or the truncation rule; paging the issue fetch.
title: release-audit: collector fails on a large open-issue backlog and hides why
